extracted.intended_audience: Registered healthcare professionals (clinicians) preparing an application for the MRC Senior Clinical Fellowship (UKRI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and assessment criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the MRC Senior Clinical Fellowship (UKRI Funding Service), including eligibility rules, required sections, word limits, assessment criteria and supporting-document requirements. Targeted at clinically registered researchers seeking support to transition to research leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (core requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply if you are a registered healthcare professional and have completed a PhD or equivalent, have experience leading research funded by a major funder, and are managing your own independent research group. You must have the skills and experience that match those of the ‘transition to leadership’ career stage in the MRC applicant skills and experience criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes, but is not limited to, nurses, midwives, allied health professionals, healthcare scientists, pharmacists, clinical psychologists, doctors, dentists, general practitioners and veterinarians (registered vets who are Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons members). Your proposed project must be relevant to human health. There are no eligibility rules based on years of postdoctoral experience. You must have the support of an eligible research organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not eligible to apply if you have previously held a comparable senior fellowship from any organisation, have applied for this MRC fellowship twice before, or have applied for another UKRI fellowship and your application is being assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot hold a salaried position and a fellowship concurrently; awardees must give up permanent position or change to a proleptic appointment for the fellowship duration. If you want to retain an existing position with combined research funding, consider other grant opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope of the fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Support internationally competitive independent investigators to lead an ambitious research programme, pursue research training to develop their career, and make the transition to research leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may cover basic to translational and clinical research across MRC remit (infections and immunity; molecular/cellular medicine; population/systems medicine; neurosciences/mental health; translation; global health; methodology; public health) and interdisciplinary/global health approaches, including longitudinal population studies with prior LPS-SAP approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor requirement and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application must identify at least one sponsor who is a senior member of the host department, acts as a supporter (not supervisor), has expertise in the research area and will act as guarantor for the quality of the proposed work, your suitability, and training received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional sponsors may be named if necessary and may be from other organisations. Sponsor statements should describe capacity in which they know you, length of relationship, views on your research ability and suitability, measures of research activity at the host, and the suitability and quality of support/training you will receive. Sponsor statement word limits and format guidance are in the 'Sponsors' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence detailing how the host organisation will support you, including who you engaged with, how the research environment contributes, how time commitment will be protected, development/training opportunities, and financial or practical support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements from head of department confirming suitability for an MRC fellowship and commitment to support. If a second host organisation or recent department change applies, include statements from relevant heads of department. Support statement up to 1,000 words; use full word count only where multiple statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core team composition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: List key members of your team and assign roles (specialist, professional enabling staff, research and innovation associate, technician, fellow). Only list one individual as fellow. At least one sponsor must be listed and assigned as professional enabling staff. Mentors should not be listed in the core team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find out more about UKRI core team roles. Project partner contact cannot be in core team roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (public-facing) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 550. In plain English, provide a summary to identify suitable experts for assessing your application; may be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe context, the challenge addressed, aims/objectives, potential applications/benefits. Make it suitable for opinion-formers, policymakers, the public and the wider research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision assessment criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 500. Explain what you hope to achieve with the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors look for evidence that the work is of excellent quality and importance within or beyond the field; potential to advance understanding or generate new knowledge; timeliness; and impacts on world-leading research, society, economy or environment. Also identify beneficiaries, potential improvements in human or population health, and plans for engagement, communication and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach assessment criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 5,500. Explain how you will deliver the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors expect design that is effective and appropriate to objectives, feasible, identifies risks and mitigation, uses clear and transparent methodology, summarises prior work and builds on it, and will maximise translation of outputs. Also demonstrate access to appropriate services/facilities/equipment, provide a detailed project plan with milestones and timelines (chart/diagram), explain collaborations and any work at a second host, justify diversity/inclusion in study populations (MRC policy), address use of both sexes in animal/tissue research or justify otherwise. You are encouraged to use 500 words (heading: 'Reproducibility and statistical design') to detail reproducibility, statistical analyses, sample sizes, models, and to seek professional statistical advice. If not applicable, do not use that space for other content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development assessment criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 1,000. Explain why this fellowship is the right way to develop your career and how you will use it to benefit others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify career development goals appropriate to the fellowship, show how the fellowship provides a feasible trajectory for your development, and how you will instigate positive change in the wider research/innovation community (EDI, advocacy, peer review, policy influence, public engagement). Describe how you will support development of those you manage (links to Concordat and Technician Commitment) and acquisition of additional skills (research, leadership, communication, management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant capability to deliver (R4RI format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 1,500 (1,000 for R4RI modules + 500 for additions if necessary). Explain why you are the right individual to deliver the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of relevant experience appropriate to career stage, balance of skills and aptitude to deliver, contributions to a positive research environment, and appropriate team working/leadership skills. Use the R4RI headings once each: contributions to generation of new ideas/tools/knowledge; development of others and working relationships; contributions to wider research/innovation community; contributions to broader research/innovation, users/audiences and societal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additions section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional up to 500 words. Provide further details relevant to your application context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use to describe additional skills, experiences, or outputs. Use for contextual factors for R4RI (for example details of career breaks if you wish to disclose them). Complete as narrative (not CV format).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical activities and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 500. Describe clinical activities/training and relation to the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include professional registration number and body (e.g., HCPC or GMC), clinical speciality/profession, current training stage (foundation, specialty registrar, consultant), completion of training date, Royal College exam details, whether you will be clinically active during/after fellowship, whether you will seek honorary clinical contract, percentage time on clinical duties (up to 20% for full-time fellowship = two clinical sessions/week; surgeons/patient-oriented projects may undertake up to four clinical sessions/week), and percentage of clinical time directly relevant to research. A downloadable template is provided to complete and paste into the text box.

rubrics_metrics.name: References section rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 1,000. List all references used to support the application in this section only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include other information. Avoid hyperlinks as assessors are not obliged to follow them; where linking use persistent identifiers (DOIs). You must not include links to extend the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors statement content and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: up to 3,000 for the section but sponsor statements should be up to 1,000 words (use full word count only if multiple sponsors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor should be senior member of host department with academic responsibility, act as supporter for application and fellowship (not supervisor), have expertise in research area and act as guarantor for quality of research and training. Each sponsor entry should detail name and position, how they know you, how long, views on your research ability/suitability, measures of research activity at base, and suitability/quality of support/training you will receive. Name sponsors in 'Core team' and assign them as professional enabling staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 500. Explain proposed mentoring arrangements during the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a mentor has been identified, they should be named and provide a statement of support detailing how they will support you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners inclusion, roles and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Project partners may support the fellowship through cash or in-kind contributions (staff time, equipment access, sites/facilities, provision of data/software/materials). Each partner must provide a statement of support. The project partner contact cannot be a named applicant or core team member. Project partner organisations cannot be applicant organisations or departments within same organisation as core team members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List organisation name, partner contact name/email, type of contribution (direct/indirect) and monetary value. If project partner responsible for recruitment or supplying human tissue, state that and include confirmations in the letter. For industry partners, additional ICF information is required. For audit purposes UKRI requires formal collaboration agreements if award is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partner letters/emails of support guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a single PDF containing letters/emails of support from each named project partner (English or Welsh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each letter/email should be no more than two A4 pages, confirm the partner’s commitment, explain value/relevance/benefits and additional value they bring, include partner organisation name and contact info (matching details entered), and may use electronic signatures. Consolidate multiple partner documents into a single PDF not exceeding 8MB. File name should use Funding Service number followed by 'Project partner'. Do not upload letters from core team members; including unrequested information may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Collaboration Framework (ICF) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 1,500. If your application includes industry project partners, answer ICF questions unless not applicable (enter 'N/A').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ICF decision tree. For each ICF partner: name the company, indicate whether the research is basic or applied, explain why the collaboration could not be undertaken without UKRI funding, state fully flexible or gated contribution category, outline background IP each partner brings and terms of access, outline expected foreground IP and how it will be managed (ownership and rights to use), outline any dissemination restrictions including rights to review/delay/remove publications, declare conflicts of interest and their management, and justify collaborating with overseas industry if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving animals requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required information and templates for animal research; certain species (non-rodent primates, cats, dogs, equines, pigs) are assessed during NC3Rs review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete NC3Rs templates or species-specific checklists as applicable, save as a single PDF and upload. For studies involving certain species the application will go through NC3Rs review. Guidance includes template links for specific species and instructions to upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving human participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 700. State whether the project involves human subjects or personal information and provide required approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable provide the name of any required approving body and whether approval is already in place. Justify number and diversity of participants and any procedures; provide details of areas of substantial or moderate severity of impact. If not applicable, indicate so in Funding Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving human tissues or biological samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 700. If using human tissues/samples provide approving body details and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide name of required approving body and whether approval is in place, justify nature and quantity of material and source. If not applicable, indicate so in Funding Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and cost justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 1,000. Justify the application’s more costly resources and explain how resources are appropriate to deliver the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on project staff, significant travel for field work/collaboration, equipment > £10,000, consumables beyond typical requirements, facilities/infrastructure costs, training costs, 'Exceptions' costs, support to work at second organisation, public and patient involvement costs, data preservation/sharing costs, NHS research costs, animal breeding/maintenance to achieve welfare standards, sponsor support (max 5% of time). Assessors do not want line-by-line detailed costs but want demonstration that resources are comprehensive, appropriate, justified and represent optimal use to achieve intended outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding, costing and permitted exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC will fund 80% of full economic cost (FEC) and 100% of permitted exceptions. There is no limit on the amount requested, but awards typically do not exceed £2 million (80% FEC). Salary contribution for the fellow may be requested at 50% of total contracted working time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expectation is 100% of contracted working time focused on research/training/development; the remaining 50% salary must be underwritten by the research organisation. This results in MRC funding 40% of total salary and 60% from the research organisation under the full economic costing framework. Sponsor costs can only be requested in exceptional circumstances (should not exceed 5% of sponsor time or 5% FTE across sponsors) and should be entered as directly allocated staff cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: What will not be funded
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC will not fund costs for PhD studentships, publication costs, funds to be used as a ‘bridge’ between grants or costs for mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requested costs do not include these excluded items; see full costing guidance for permitted exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and part-time rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship provides support for up to five years and applicants are expected to take advantage of the full five years. Awards may be held part-time to meet personal commitments but not because of other professional commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests from GPs, nurses, midwives, allied health professionals and other non-medic healthcare professionals to undertake part-time awards to continue professional clinical responsibilities may be considered. Medically qualified applicants may not apply for part-time awards to continue higher specialist training during the fellowship. Fellows should take up their award no more than six months after interview. Up to twelve months of the award may be spent at a second organisation (UK, overseas or industry). If intending long overseas periods, contact fellows@mrc.ukri.org before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project plan and visuals rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project plan, milestones and timelines should be provided, and visual elements may be used sparingly where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may demonstrate elements in visual form if relevant; use images sparingly only to convey information that cannot easily be expressed in words. Insert each new image on a new line; provide a descriptive legend immediately underneath each image (counts towards word limit). Ensure files are <5MB and in accepted formats (JPEG/JPG/JPE/JFI/JIF/JFIF/PNG/GIF/BMP/WEBP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners declaration and audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For audit purposes UKRI requires formal collaboration agreements with project partners if an award is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure partner details and letters match and that project partners will provide support as indicated. If details are entered incorrectly in the Funding Service, remove the record and re-add it with correct information for audit trail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research using NHS resources and SoECAT
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 250. If research takes place in NHS or public health/social care setting and intends NIHR CRN portfolio inclusion, a Schedule of Events Cost Attribution Tool (SoECAT) must be completed and uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include contacting an AcoRD specialist, completing online SoECAT, requesting authorisation, converting the funder export 'study information' and 'summary' pages into a single PDF and uploading. Applications that require a SoECAT but have not attached the funder export may be rejected. Contact fellows@mrc.ukri.org with SoECAT concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related applications disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 500. Declare if this application is related to another application to MRC or another funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If related, explain how the new application is related. If it is a resubmission include previous MRC reference and describe differences and how previous feedback was addressed. You may apply for fellowship funding from other funders at the same time, but you may only apply twice for any MRC fellowship in total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint funder declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Word limit: 20. Declare if you are applying for a jointly-funded fellowship and provide the joint funder name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting a joint funder agrees to MRC sharing this application and personal information with the joint funder. Available options include Diabetes UK, MRC-Motor Neurone Disease Association Lady Edith Wolfson fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process overview (peer review, shortlisting, interview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed by peer review, shortlisted applications go to an interview panel; shortlisted applicants are invited to interview and may respond to review comments during interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortlisting panel reviews comments and scores. If not shortlisted, applicants receive review comments but cannot respond. Interviews typically last 45 minutes for clinical training and career development panel. MRC aims to communicate decisions within ten days of shortlisting meeting and to complete assessment process within six months of receiving application. MRC makes the final funding decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment areas (explicit evaluation dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment areas used are: vision for the fellowship; approach to the fellowship; career development; your capability to deliver the fellowship (skills and experience needed at this career stage); support for the applicant; ethical and responsible research and innovation considerations; resources requested to do the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment will take into account career breaks, flexible working and changes in discipline when assessing career development and capability to deliver. See individual 'Application questions' sections for detailed assessment questions and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of assessment and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC supports the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA) and recognises the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment and decision-making should follow UKRI principles of assessment and decision making. Reviewers and panels are advised to consider research integrity and DORA principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission, platform and procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via the new UKRI Funding Service (not Je-S). The fellow is responsible for completing the application, but the lead research organisation submits it through its research office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign in or create a Funding Service account, select host organisation early (allow 10 working days for organisation to be added), answer questions in text boxes (can save and return or work offline and paste), upload documents where indicated following format/size rules. Allow time for research office checking and submission; once submitted applications cannot be changed. If guidance not followed, application may be rejected. Where indicated, elements may be demonstrated visually (see image/file rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents: format, limits and content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific supporting documents (project partner letters, SoECAT funder export, animal templates, sponsor/host statements) must follow stated formats, page limits and file size rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project partner letters: max two A4 pages each, consolidated single PDF <8MB. Images: files <5MB and accepted image types. Host and sponsor support statements: defined word limits. Do not include unrequested letters or extra supporting information; inclusion of unrequested information may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and sensitive information processes
rubrics_metrics.description: If application is discussed by a panel, feedback will be provided with the outcome. Sensitive/confidential information should be emailed to fellows@mrc.ukri.org with specified subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you reach interview stage you will receive review comments and reasons for panel decisions. If not invited to interview you will be sent review comments. Sensitive information examples: individual unavailable until a date, declaration of interest, additional eligibility info not appropriate for application text, conflicts for UKRI to consider. See UKRI privacy notice for personal data processing.
